blog.wedding-slow-motion-effect.p_text.a: AI frame interpolation has changed everything. In 2026, you can add stunning slow motion to virtually any wedding video, regardless of how it was originally filmed. Here's how.

AI frame interpolation takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of mathematically estimating pixel movement, it uses deep neural networks trained on millions of video frames to understand what objects look like, how they move, and what the space between two frames should actually contain.

analyzes pixel movement between frames and generates intermediate positions. It's better than frame blending but produces visible artifacts around fast-moving objects, edges, and areas where objects appear or disappear.

blog.wedding-slow-motion-effect.p_text.t: Technically, you can slow footage down as much as you want, but quality degrades with extreme slowdowns. For most wedding footage, 2-4x slowdown produces the best balance of dramatic effect and visual quality. Beyond 6-8x, even AI interpolation starts to show artifacts, and the footage can feel unnaturally slow.

The fundamental problem: traditional methods are trying to guess what happened between two frames based on mathematical models. They don't understand the content of the video.

The results are often indistinguishable from footage that was natively shot at high frame rates. In blind tests, professional editors frequently cannot tell AI-interpolated slow motion from genuine 120fps footage.
